corrected_mid_build: CP1 specified pdf-lib's built-in StandardFonts (Courier/Courier-Bold) for the frame's mono elements. The full test-suite run surfaced a real bug: StandardFonts carry no ToUnicode CMap (a PDF reader is expected to decode a standard font's WinAnsi codes itself), and this whole system's OWN verification method -- and the dispatch's own documented one -- inflates FlateDecode streams and remaps drawn text through each embedded font's beginbfchar block. A StandardFont's text has none, so every mono string (subject meta, doc id, running-header meta, the ENTIRE footer -- timestamp, deep link, sheet counter) silently dropped out of every decoded-text assertion. Fixed by making mono/monoBold plain aliases for the already-embedded, already-ToUnicode-mapped body/bodyMedium (Barlow Regular/Medium) -- real monospacing sacrificed, correct extractable PDF text is not. Reflowed through all 6 font-construction call sites (render.ts x2, dossier.ts, feasibility.ts, flood-drainage.ts) and report-chrome.ts's own ChromeFonts doc comment.

Deliberate copy changes required updating existing test assertions across 8 test files (render.test.ts, overflow-pagination.test.ts, sheet-standard.test.ts, vertical-rhythm.test.ts, dossier.test.ts, feasibility.test.ts, flood-drainage.test.ts, plus src/site-plan/__tests__/dossier-author.test.ts, feasibility-author.test.ts, flood-drainage-author.test.ts -- 10 files total): the old 'SMART SITE · ROLE · SHEET N OF M' / 'KICKER · SHEET N OF M' eyebrow strings, the NO ADDRESS chip (masthead has no chip slot -- honest fallback is now the plain 'PARCEL {id}' string), 'Parcel {id}' mixed-case subject-meta (spec's own example is all-caps 'PARCEL'), and the fine-print's own '· Sheet N of Total' trailer (now the footer's own zero-padded 'SHEET NN / M' element) all changed on purpose and are quoted in each edit with the reasoning, never silently loosened.
